# ForEach

Header: `winui/ui/collections/ForEach.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/collections/ForEach.hpp`.

A repeater: a collection laid out by an attachable [Layout](item-layouts.md#uilayout) that realizes only the items in view.

It has no chrome, selection or scrolling of its own. Put it in a [Scroll](../layout/scroll.md#uiscroll) and it asks its item template only for the items its layout places in the viewport and a cache buffer around it, and destroys the rest as they scroll away. The collection is an index range ([set_item_count()](#set_item_count)) that the template turns into elements. The repeater owns every realized element. Report collection changes with the notify_*() calls so realized elements stay with their items. [ListView](list-view.md#uilistview) and [TileView](tile-view.md#uitileview) are built on it. Use it directly for a custom collection without chrome.

Example: 
```cpp
// Declarative: 500 cards in a wrap layout, inside a scroller.
std::vector<std::string> names;
for (int i = 0; i < 500; ++i)
    names.push_back(std::format("Card {}", i));
window.set_content(ui::Scroll{
    .height  = 320.0f,
    .content = ui::ForEach<std::string>{
        .items      = names,
        .layout     = ui::WrapLayout{},
        .virtualize = true,
        .item       = [](const std::string& name) -> ui::Spec {
            return ui::Text{.text = name, .width = 96.0f, .height = 64.0f};
        },
    },
});

// Imperative:
std::vector<std::string> rows{"First", "Second", "Third"};
auto  scroll   = std::make_unique<ui::ScrollControl>();
auto* repeater = scroll->set_child(std::make_unique<ui::ForEachControl>());
repeater->set_layout(std::make_unique<ui::StackLayoutEngine>())->set_spacing(4.0f);
repeater->set_item_template([&rows](std::size_t i) { return std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>(rows[i]); });
repeater->set_item_count(rows.size());
repeater->on_element_prepared([](const ui::ElementPreparedArgs& args) { std::println("realized {}", args.index); });

rows.insert(rows.begin(), "New first row");
repeater->notify_inserted(0);
```

## `ui::ForEach`

A repeater: turns a collection into children, and nothing else. Builds a [ui::ForEachControl](#uiforeachcontrol).

[`.items`](#uiforeach-items) is the collection, [`.item`](#uiforeach-item) is how one of them looks, and [`.layout`](#uiforeach-layout) is how they are arranged, a vertical stack when left out. It has no selection, keyboard navigation or scrolling of its own. For those, use a view such as [ui::ListView](list-view.md#uilistview), [ui::TileView](tile-view.md#uitileview) or [ui::TableView](table-view.md#uitableview). To scroll a [ForEach](#uiforeach), put it in a [ui::Scroll](../layout/scroll.md#uiscroll). To mix fixed and generated children, put the [ForEach](#uiforeach) in an ordinary stack next to the fixed ones.

By default every item is built and stays built, wherever the [ForEach](#uiforeach) sits. A row keeps its own state, such as a text box's text, for as long as its item is in the collection. Set [`.virtualize = true`](#uiforeach-virtualize) for long collections inside a [ui::Scroll](../layout/scroll.md#uiscroll). Then only the rows in and near view exist, and a row's state is lost when it scrolls away, so keep that state in the item.

[`.items`](#uiforeach-items) takes one of three sources, and they differ in how a change reaches the rows:

- A [ui::ObservableVector<T>](../core/observable-vector.md) ([`.items = todos`](#uiforeach-items)), for a collection the app edits in place. Each insert builds one row and each removal destroys one. A move keeps the row's element and moves it, and a replacement builds that one row again. [`.item`](#uiforeach-item) receives the item as `T&`. It may keep that reference and bind to the item's own [Property](../core/property.md) members, because an item stays at its address for as long as it is in the collection.
- A [`ui::Property<std::vector<T>>`](../core/property.md) ([`.items = photos`](#uiforeach-items)), for a collection the app assigns as a whole, for example after loading, filtering or sorting it. With [`.key`](#uiforeach-key), the old and the new keys are compared. A row whose key is still there keeps its element and state wherever it moved to, and is built again only when its item compares unequal. A change that needs very many moves, such as a shuffle of several thousand items, arrives as one reset instead, which builds every row again. Without [`.key`](#uiforeach-key), the rows before and after the edit are kept and those in between are built again. That covers appending, inserting or removing a run of items, but not a reorder. The rows read a copy of the collection the control owns, so [`.item`](#uiforeach-item) must not keep the reference it is given.
- A plain `std::vector<T>`, copied once, for a fixed collection.

Name the item type, as in [`ui::ForEach<Photo>`](#uiforeach). C++ deduces a spec's type only from the field's own type, which a [Property](../core/property.md) or an [ObservableVector](../core/observable-vector.md) is not.

Lifetime: [`.item`](#uiforeach-item) is stored on the built control and called for the life of the tree, so it must not capture anything shorter-lived than the window.

Example: 
```cpp
struct Photo
{
    int         id = 0;
    std::string title;
    friend bool operator==(const Photo&, const Photo&) = default;
};
ui::Property<std::vector<Photo>> photos{{{1, "Lake"}, {2, "Bridge"}, {3, "Harbor"}}};

window.set_content(ui::Scroll{.content = ui::ForEach<Photo>{
    .items  = photos,
    .key    = &Photo::id,
    .layout = ui::TileLayout{.min_item_width = 160.0f, .min_row_spacing = 8.0f, .min_column_spacing = 8.0f},
    .item   = [](const Photo& p) -> ui::Spec { return ui::Text{.text = p.title}; },
}});

std::vector<Photo> sorted = photos.get();
std::ranges::sort(sorted, {}, &Photo::title);
photos = sorted; // the rows move, none is built again
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::ForEach{
    .items, .key, .layout, .virtualize, .horizontal_cache_length, .vertical_cache_length,
    .item_transitions, .background, .style, .margin, .width, .height, .min_width, .min_height,
    .max_width, .max_height, .horizontal_alignment, .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip,
    .accessibility, .on_element_prepared, .on_element_clearing, .on_element_index_changed,
    .on_pointer_entered, .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus, .on_key_down,
    .on_wheel, .control, .item
}
```

Fields, in declaration order (designators must follow it):

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="uiforeach-items"></span>`items` | `ui::Binding<std::vector<T>>` |  | The collection. A [ui::ObservableVector<T>](../core/observable-vector.md) or a [`ui::Property<std::vector<T>>`](../core/property.md) is followed as it changes. A plain vector is copied once. |
| <span id="uiforeach-key"></span>`key` | `ui::ItemKey<std::type_identity_t<T>>` |  | What identifies an item when [`.items`](#uiforeach-items) is bound to a [`ui::Property<std::vector<T>>`](../core/property.md): a member pointer or a callable returning the key. With it, a row follows its item through any reorder. Keys must be unique. A collection that repeats one is rebuilt as a whole, and a debug build asserts. Not needed with a [ui::ObservableVector](../core/observable-vector.md). |
| <span id="uiforeach-layout"></span>`layout` | `ui::LayoutSpec` |  | How the items are arranged; a vertical stack when left out. |
| <span id="uiforeach-virtualize"></span>`virtualize` | `bool` | `false` | When false, every item is built and keeps its state. When true, only the rows in and near view are built, for a long collection inside a [ui::Scroll](../layout/scroll.md#uiscroll). A row's state is then lost when it scrolls away. |
| <span id="uiforeach-horizontal_cache_length"></span>`horizontal_cache_length` | `ui::Binding<float>` | `{2.0f}` | With [`virtualize`](#uiforeach-virtualize): how many viewports' worth of rows to keep built beyond the one in view, split evenly before and after it. 2, one on each side, by default; 0 builds only what shows. |
| <span id="uiforeach-vertical_cache_length"></span>`vertical_cache_length` | `ui::Binding<float>` | `{2.0f}` | See [`horizontal_cache_length`](#uiforeach-horizontal_cache_length). |
| <span id="uiforeach-item_transitions"></span>`item_transitions` | `ui::TransitionList` |  | Transitions every row runs. With a [ui::AddRemoveTransition](../tree/element-transitions.md#struct-addremovetransition) an inserted row grows in, a removed one shrinks away and the rows after it slide into place. |
| <span id="uiforeach-background"></span>`background` | `ui::Binding<ui::Paint>` |  | Background behind the rows: a fixed color, or a theme color that follows theme switches. Unset draws none. |
| <span id="uiforeach-on_element_prepared"></span>`on_element_prepared` | `ui::Callback<void(const ui::ElementPreparedArgs&)>` |  | A row was built for the item at this position, before it is measured. With [`virtualize`](#uiforeach-virtualize) that happens as rows scroll into view. |
| <span id="uiforeach-on_element_clearing"></span>`on_element_clearing` | `ui::Callback<void(ui::Element&)>` |  | A row is about to be destroyed because it scrolled out, its item was removed, or the collection was reset. |
| <span id="uiforeach-on_element_index_changed"></span>`on_element_index_changed` | `ui::Callback<void(const ui::ElementIndexChangedArgs&)>` |  | A change of the collection moved a row's item, with the old and the new position. |
| <span id="uiforeach-on_pointer_entered"></span>`on_pointer_entered` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer moved onto the control. |
| <span id="uiforeach-on_pointer_exited"></span>`on_pointer_exited` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer left the control. |
| <span id="uiforeach-on_got_focus"></span>`on_got_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus arrived on the control, or on anything inside it, from outside it. A control with nothing focusable in it never gets focus, and never raises this. |
| <span id="uiforeach-on_lost_focus"></span>`on_lost_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus left the control and everything inside it. |
| <span id="uiforeach-on_key_down"></span>`on_key_down` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::KeyEvent&)>` |  | A key pressed while focus is on the control or inside it, before the control's own handling; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_key_down()](../tree/element.md#on_key_down)). |
| <span id="uiforeach-on_wheel"></span>`on_wheel` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::PointerEvent&)>` |  | A wheel turn over the control, before the control scrolls; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_wheel()](../tree/element.md#on_wheel)). |
| <span id="uiforeach-control"></span>`control` | `ui::ControlOut<std::type_identity_t<ui::ForEach>>` |  | Out: the handle that receives the built control. Its type uses std::type_identity_t, so passing a handle does not take part in deducing the type argument. |
| <span id="uiforeach-item"></span>`item` | `ui::Callback<ui::Spec(std::type_identity_t<T>&)>` |  | How one item looks: a callable taking `const T&`, or `T&` to edit an item of a [ui::ObservableVector](../core/observable-vector.md). Its type uses std::type_identity_t, so [`.items`](#uiforeach-items) alone decides T when the type argument is left out. |

Plus the common fields `style`, `margin`, `width`, `height`, `min_width`, `min_height`, `max_width`, `max_height`, `horizontal_alignment`, `vertical_alignment`, `visible`, `tool_tip`, `accessibility` every spec carries ([conventions](../conventions.md#common-fields-on-every-spec)).

### build

```cpp
std::unique_ptr<Element> build()&&
```

Consumes the spec and returns the built [ui::ForEachControl](#uiforeachcontrol); the caller owns it.

## `ui::ForEachControl`

Derives from `ui::Element`, `ui::LayoutOwner`.

It has no chrome, selection or scrolling of its own. ### ItemTemplate

```cpp
using ui::ForEachControl::ItemTemplate = Callback<std::unique_ptr<Element>(std::size_t index)>
```

Makes the element for item `index` and may choose a different look per item. Called when the item is realized. The repeater owns what it returns.

### ForEachControl

```cpp
ForEachControl()
```

An empty repeater with a default [StackLayoutEngine](item-layouts.md#class-stacklayoutengine) and cache lengths of 2.


### set_item_template

```cpp
void set_item_template(ItemTemplate item_template)
```

Replaces the template. Every realized element is cleared and made again.

### has_item_template

```cpp
bool has_item_template() const
```

Whether an item template is set. Without one nothing is realized.

### item_count

```cpp
std::size_t item_count() const
```

How many items the collection holds.

### set_item_count

```cpp
void set_item_count(std::size_t count)
```

Replaces the collection with `count` new items (a reset).

### notify_inserted

```cpp
void notify_inserted(std::size_t index, std::size_t count = 1)
```

Reports that `count` items were inserted at `index`.

### notify_removed

```cpp
void notify_removed(std::size_t index, std::size_t count = 1)
```

Reports that `count` items were removed from `index`. With an [AddRemoveTransition](../tree/element-transitions.md#struct-addremovetransition) among the [children_transitions()](../tree/element.md#children_transitions), each removed element fades out in place before it is destroyed.

### notify_replaced

```cpp
void notify_replaced(std::size_t index, std::size_t count = 1)
```

Reports that `count` items at `index` were replaced. Their elements are made again.

### notify_moved

```cpp
void notify_moved(std::size_t from, std::size_t to)
```

Reports that one item moved from `from` to `to`, its position after the move. Its element moves with it.

### notify_reset

```cpp
void notify_reset()
```

Reports any other change: the whole collection is new, with the same count.

### set_layout

```cpp
template <typename T>
T* set_layout(std::unique_ptr<T> layout)
```

Takes ownership of the layout and returns an observer. Replaces the previous layout and clears every realized element. nullptr restores the default [StackLayoutEngine](item-layouts.md#class-stacklayoutengine).

### layout

```cpp
Layout* layout() const
```

The current layout, non-owning and never nullptr.

### set_background

```cpp
void set_background(std::optional<Color> color)
```

Background behind the items, as a fixed color; nullopt (the default) draws none. Redraws.

### set_background

```cpp
void set_background(ThemeColor resource)
```

Background as a theme color, read again when the theme changes. Redraws.

### horizontal_cache_length

```cpp
float horizontal_cache_length() const
```

How many viewports' worth of items to keep realized beyond the one in view, split evenly before and after it. 2 by default, one on each side. 0 realizes only what shows.

Sets the horizontal cache length and lays the repeater out again.


Sets the vertical cache length and lays the repeater out again.


### automation_role

```cpp
AutomationRole automation_role() const override
```

What screen readers and other assistive tools see of this node: the role, name, help text and children here, and what a client can do with the node through the providers [automation_providers()](../tree/element.md#automation_providers) lists (ui/Automation.hpp).

[automation_role()](#automation_role) is the role this node reports; Group by default.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

Implement these instead of [measure()](../tree/element.md#measure) and [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange). The base class has already applied margin, size limits and alignment by the time these run. [measure_override()](#measure_override) is pure (every concrete [Element](../tree/element.md) must size itself); [arrange_override()](#arrange_override) defaults to a no-op since most leaves need nothing beyond having [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds) set, which the base already did.

### arrange_override

```cpp
void arrange_override(const Rect& final_rect, const ArrangeContext& context) override
```

Position children within the rect [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange) settled on (also in [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds), window DIPs). Default: nothing, for a leaf.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

What the control draws, in layout coordinates; [render()](../tree/element.md#render) has already applied the visual layer. A container draws its children through their [render()](../tree/element.md#render), never their [render_override()](#render_override).

### tick_override

```cpp
void tick_override(Duration delta) override
```

Advances the background and exit transitions, then ticks a snapshot of the realized elements. A child's handler may change the collection. An element recycled or cleared on the way is skipped.

## struct ElementPreparedArgs

What `on_element_prepared` gets: an element about to show item [`index`](#struct-elementpreparedargs).

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `element` | `Element&` |  | The realized element. |
| `index` | `std::size_t` |  | The item it shows. |

## struct ElementIndexChangedArgs

What `on_element_index_changed` gets: an element whose item moved.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `element` | `Element&` |  | The realized element. |
| `old_index` | `std::size_t` |  | Where its item was. |
| `new_index` | `std::size_t` |  | Where its item is now. |
